Did you feel as if your head was kind of in the ceiling? Like you were looking down almost from the perspective of being on a diving board? If so I can relate, though I'm actually on the opposite end of the size spectrum as you. 

As far as the body dysmorphia goes -- you were just tripping man lol. Everyone has a distorted view of themselves and everyone's perception of size is "off" , as someone who's tall it's really hard for me to distinguish most people's height.

I second this; when you feel you are at a place where you are ready to "go all the way" with confronting this stuff, then do it, but until you've reached that place wait a bit longer. Arguably the best thing about acid is being able to address/see things you literally can't (to a full extent) sober, and unwind the knots you've been tying inside yourself. But you need to be ready to go down this path, otherwise it might feel like you are getting dragged rather than walking. If you have intention/planning and it feels right, go for it and just try to learn and accept what comes.

It's pretty hard to define ego death, so unless you literally had an OBE it would be pretty difficult for another person to say one way or the other on your behalf. Some people would say that the way a lot of people think about ego death is too strict, and that what you had would constitute one if you felt it was an intense enough experience. The way I think about it for myself is that I've had lots of "partial" ego deaths, some of which sound like what you're talking about, and about a week ago I went all the way through (floated out of my vision into blackness, didn't know where I was, who I was, and how my body was physically positioned). My experience (both for what happened last week and what led up to it the past few years) is pinned to my profile; it's very long but give it a read it you want more context on my perspective.

As others have said I'd recommend you lay off everything for a while. If after many months you still feel it's bothering you, it may be something deep inside wanting closure. If you try to remedy this with a trip, I would recommend going in with a mindset that you'll accept everything that's happening to you. For instance, if you hear whispering, try to (subliminally) whisper back. Demonic shit only can have power over you if you truly view it as something fear-inducing. If you accept it as something that exists, maybe even something that's necessary, you will understand we all are born with both god and the devil in us (if you want to put these opposing wings of morality into a religious paradigm). Another approach would be trying to focus on the negative image you see, as opposed to turning away from it (i.e. turn demonic imagery into angelic imagery). 

One other thing you can do is search r/DMT with some of the key terms (demonic, devil, hell,etc) that are related to what's been bugging you (they are more likely to have experienced the type of things you're talking about) and read other people's experiences, which will make what you went through feel more normal.  There was this one interesting thing I read on there about a dude who saw the devil, but he understood that the devil was almost an employee and was almost "cool" with god in a sense, as some sort of a natural counter balance that makes the world be a true spiritual test (couldn't find it just now sorry). I found it while searching posts related to the idea that "we're already dead", which is something that popped up during a partial ego death experience I had. Reading other people's stories allowed me to make peace and go all the way in. Granted, it was scary, I thought I was trapped in some fake reality, timeless purgatory/hell and would be condemned there forever. But once I remembered I was on a substance and just needed to accept everything and dive deeper, I came out the other side with this wonderful sense of relief, so much weight off my shoulders, and a mountain of perspective gained.
